# Interface contracts

Detailed contracts retained from the scientific integration work. For current selections and build commands, start with the [interface guide](README.md). Historical evidence describes its own source snapshot.

## Inputs and generated files

For complex checked Cholesky on Apple arm64, select
`-Dchecked-complex-cholesky=true` with `install-abplas-lp64` or
`install-checked-sparse`. This additive frontend uses the same Core, default
Context, scalar types and admitted Cholesky implementation. It creates no factor
handle, allocator or thread pool. The original checked-v1 eight declarations,
descriptor layouts and existing status values remain unchanged.

The installed `<zynum/checked/cholesky.h>` includes the real declarations and
adds `zynum_checked_cholesky_factor_complex_f32`,
`zynum_checked_cholesky_factor_complex_f64` and the corresponding `solve`
functions. `<zynum/checked/complex.h>` owns the shared `re, im` pair types used
by both this frontend and `<zynum/checked/sparse.h>`; either include order is
valid. Buffer lengths count scalar elements, including complex pairs, rather
than bytes. Checked descriptors are column-major. Ordinary LAPACKE POTRF/POTRS
retains its separate row/column-major and IEEE/INFO contracts.

Keep the factor allocation alive across solves; each solve leaves it unchanged.
Selected entries must be finite and Hermitian diagonal imaginary parts must be
exactly zero. A nonreal diagonal returns
`ZYNUM_CHECKED_CHOLESKY_INVALID_HERMITIAN_DIAGONAL` (15), with zero `info` and
`reserved`. Argument/finite/diagonal-form rejection precedes mutation; numerical
failure can retain a completed prefix and reports a one-based position. Other
triangles and padding are ignored and preserved. Factor storage is owned by the
caller and has no dependency on an ended operation or a closed internal Context.

```sh
python3 tools/generate_checked_cholesky.py --profile checked-cholesky-v1 \
  --target-contract apple-arm64-default-c-v1 --check
zig build install-abplas-lp64 -Doptimize=ReleaseFast \
  -Dblas-interface=lp64 -Dfft-interface=fftw3 -Dlapacke-qr=true \
  -Dlapacke-complex-gelsd=true -Dlapacke-svd=true -Dsparse-solves=true \
  -Doperator-interface=zynum_v1 -Doperator-phase-agreement=true \
  -Dchecked-complex-cholesky=true --prefix /absolute/empty/prefix
zig build test-checked-cholesky-profile test-checked-cholesky-lifecycle \
  -Dtest-optimize=ReleaseSafe
```

The Cholesky generator profile and `checked_complex_cholesky` pkg-config field
record this selection. Omission defaults to false and adds no complex Cholesky
exports. Use a fresh prefix when changing selections. Generation/manifests
describe the finite declaration contract; they do not establish other targets,
Fortran complex entrypoints, full LAPACK coverage or ABP production use of POTRS.

`tools/numerical_operation_schema.py` defines mathematical operation roles;
`tools/checked_abi_profile.py` defines the checked declarations, fixed 64-bit
layout, status mapping and eight bindings. `tools/checked_abi_schema.py` selects
and validates those inputs. `tools/generate_checked_abi.py` produces the C
header, ISO_C_BINDING module, Zig types/exports, ABI manifest and Windows export
definition. The layout model is explicit and independent of the Python
generator host. Change the operation/profile inputs or generator and regenerate;
never hand-edit the outputs. `implementation.zig` supplies checked adapters.
Run from the repository root:

```sh
python3 tools/generate_checked_abi.py
python3 tools/generate_checked_abi.py --check
python3 tools/generate_checked_abi.py --profile checked-v1 --check
zig build install-checked-abi -Dcpu=baseline
zig build test-checked-abi -Dcpu=baseline -Dtest-optimize=safe
zig build test-checked-fortran -Dcpu=baseline -Dtest-optimize=safe
```

Use `zig build -Dchecked-abi=true` to include these files in the default installation, or `install-checked-abi` to install only this interface. The C header is `<zynum/checked/checked.h>`; the Fortran source is installed at `include/zynum/checked/checked.f90`. Compile that source with the consumer's own Fortran compiler; compiler-specific `.mod` files are not shipped. Link the separate `zynum_checked` shared or static library, optionally through `pkg-config zynum_checked`.

Omitting `--profile` selects `checked-v1`, with identical generated bytes.
Selecting a complete `mkl2026.lp64` or `mkl2026.ilp64` profile without a finite
binding set still fails before formatting or artifact writes. A reserved profile
name does not establish complete vendor compatibility.

## Optional ordinary TRTRI inverse

On the finite Apple arm64 target, `-Dlapacke-trtri=true` adds `LAPACKE_strtri`,
`dtrtri`, `ctrtri`, `ztrtri` and their `_work` entries to the LP64/ILP64
standalone and unified LP64 installation targets. It defaults to false.
Both levels take layout, uplo, diag, n, writable A and lda; `_work` has no
caller workspace parameters. LP64 and ILP64 remain separate integer-width
artifacts. Include the installed width-specific header and link its matching
package, or use an original compatible MKL header first.

All four scalars support upper/lower, unit/nonunit diagonals and row/column
layouts. The selected triangle receives its inverse. Unit diagonal entries,
the opposite triangle and padding remain unchanged; a unit diagonal is not
read, including by the optional high-level NaN scan. High-level A NaNs return
-5; work entries skip this scan. A first exactly zero nonunit diagonal returns
its one-based positive INFO before any inverse store and preserves A.

The pure native-sized numerical core borrows widened workspace: none for an
empty or singleton matrix, otherwise n existing wide scalar values. A complete
inverse column is evaluated before narrowing. The adapter acquires this space
through the existing operation's Scratch service. Column-major calls use at
most one lease; row-major calls use at most two, including transposition.
Intrinsic workspace OOM returns -1010 and transpose OOM returns -1011. Copyback
completes before either free callback and before the admitted operation ends.
No allocator, thread pool, handle registry or execution owner is introduced.
Selected extreme representable cases are qualified; this is not a guarantee
for every ill-conditioned range or a vendor's nonfinite payloads/FP flags.

With the other ordinary additions selected as below, standalone LP64 exposes
116 numerical functions plus two diagnostics and ILP64 exposes 72 plus two.
The selected unified LP64 candidate has 690 public symbols. There are 118
reviewed generation selections, including 60 TRTRI compositions. Their source
generation contracts do not establish runtime acceptance of every selection
or a complete MKL profile.

```sh
zig build install-lapacke-lp64 install-lapacke-ilp64 \
  -Dcpu=baseline -Doptimize=ReleaseFast \
  -Dlapacke-qr=true -Dlapacke-complex-gelsd=true -Dlapacke-svd=true \
  -Dlapacke-posv=true -Dlapacke-trtrs=true -Dlapacke-trtri=true \
  --prefix /absolute/empty/prefix
zig build test-lapacke-trtri-profile test-lapack test-numerics-contract \
  -Dcpu=baseline -Dtest-optimize=ReleaseSafe
```

## Optional ordinary TRTRS solve

On the finite Apple arm64 target, `-Dlapacke-trtrs=true` adds `LAPACKE_strtrs`,
`dtrtrs`, `ctrtrs`, `ztrtrs` and their `_work` entries to
`install-lapacke-lp64`, `install-lapacke-ilp64` and `install-abplas-lp64`.
It defaults to false. Both levels take layout, uplo, trans, diag, n, nrhs,
const A, lda, writable B and ldb; neither accepts an explicit workspace.
LP64 uses C `int`, and the separate ILP64 artifact uses C `long long int`.
Link one integer-width interface per consumer.

All four scalar families support upper/lower, N/T/C, unit/nonunit diagonal,
and row/column layouts. A is preserved and B receives the solution. A unit
diagonal is not read, including during the optional high-level NaN scan.
With `nrhs=0`, nonunit calls still scan for the first exactly zero diagonal
and return its one-based positive INFO; unit column-major calls need no
operand access. Positive INFO preserves B. This ordinary IEEE implementation
does not promise a vendor's nonfinite values, payloads or exception flags.

High-level validation checks layout, then optionally scans the selected A
triangle and B. NaNs report -7 and -9 respectively. Work entries skip the NaN
scan. Column-major argument errors retain the LAPACKE one-position shift;
row-major lda/ldb rejection reports -8/-10. Row-major staging borrows two
scratch leases from one admitted operation, with reverse cleanup and -1011
on allocation failure. The operation remains live through callbacks and B
copyback. There is no new handle registry, allocator or worker pool.

The common triangular core also supplies the existing LU solve's substitutions.
Its LU RHS bytes were checked against the previous implementation in Debug,
ReleaseSafe and ReleaseFast, including zero/nonfinite cases. The internal
core uses native-sized descriptors and the existing real/complex types;
external integer widths are confined to the adapters.

With POSV, QR, complex GELSD and SVD also selected, standalone LP64 contains
108 numerical functions and ILP64 contains 64; each shared artifact adds its
two existing diagnostic exports. The generator accepts 24 reviewed additive
TRTRS selections alongside the 34 prior finite selections. Generation-only
combinations do not imply installed runtime acceptance for every selection or
complete MKL compatibility.

```sh
zig build install-lapacke-lp64 install-lapacke-ilp64 \
  -Dcpu=baseline -Doptimize=ReleaseFast \
  -Dlapacke-qr=true -Dlapacke-complex-gelsd=true -Dlapacke-svd=true \
  -Dlapacke-posv=true -Dlapacke-trtrs=true --prefix /absolute/empty/prefix
zig build test-lapacke-trtrs-profile test-lapack test-numerics-contract \
  -Dcpu=baseline -Dtest-optimize=ReleaseSafe
```

## Optional ordinary POSV driver

On Apple arm64, `-Dlapacke-posv=true` adds `LAPACKE_sposv`, `dposv`,
`cposv`, `zposv` and their `_work` entries to the selected finite LAPACKE
package. It applies to `install-lapacke-lp64`, `install-lapacke-ilp64` and the
LP64 `install-abplas-lp64` package, and defaults to false. The high and work
signatures both take layout, triangle, n, nrhs, writable A, lda, writable B and
ldb; `_work` has no explicit workspace arguments. LP64 uses C `int` and ILP64
uses C `long long int`, with the same ordinary symbol names in separate
libraries. Link one width per consumer.

The default LP64 selection has 64 numerical entries with POSV enabled; its
optional QR, complex GELSD and SVD combination has 100. ILP64 has 56. The two
smaller explicitly generated `potrf-potrs-posv-ordinary-{lp64,ilp64}-v1`
selections each contain 24 entries. The generation script accepts only the
11 reviewed POSV combinations, the original target contract and unchanged
complex pair layouts; this does not enable a complete vendor profile.

POSV admits one operation from the existing Context, validates the whole driver
contract, then calls the existing ordinary POTRF and POTRS numerical cores.
Row-major staging uses that operation's two existing scratch leases. The
operation stays live through callbacks, factor/RHS copyback and reverse cleanup.
There is no new factor handle, numerical owner, allocator or worker pool.

High-level calls scan the selected A triangle then B when NaN checking is
internally enabled; work calls do not scan. A NaN reports -5, a B NaN reports
-7. `nrhs=0` still factors A. Positive INFO preserves B and may leave a partial
factor in A; its failed A bytes follow the own unblocked core and are not
promised to equal a vendor's recursive implementation. Ordinary finite complex
diagonal imaginary parts are ignored, retaining the separate ordinary contract.
The factor remains caller-owned and can be reused by POTRS after return.
The finite package still does not export LAPACKE NaN-control functions.

The isolated candidate passed Debug/ReleaseSafe/ReleaseFast orchestration,
C/C++ static/shared LP64/ILP64 clients, scaled residual/reconstruction and
factor-reuse checks, and inclusion after the pinned MKL 2026 header. Main
promotion, a fresh installation and 28 installed client processes have since
completed. These include unified-package and live-FFT-plan lifetime regression
across BLAS shutdown/reinitialization. The actual Main ABPLaS replay also passed
the three cases described above; it has no POSV call and establishes regression
of its existing dependency paths. This addition is external interface coverage.
The full Python tooling sweeps are a separate acceptance step.

The installed finite selections are
`potrf-potrs-getrf-getrs-gesv-stev-gelsd-ordinary-{lp64,ilp64}-v1`, each containing 48
ordinary high-level/work entrypoints. `potrf`, `potrs`, `getrf`, `getrs` and
`gesv` cover four scalar types; `stev` and `gelsd` cover real single/double precision. They require `apple-arm64-default-c-v1`,
default complex layout, matching integer width and the reviewed source/plan
fingerprints. The previous 32-, 40- and 44-entrypoint selections remain accepted for
explicit generation, but the install targets now package the 48-entrypoint
selections. The smaller 16-symbol selections and explicit `_64` symbols remain
unaccepted.

On Apple arm64, install one integer-width package explicitly:

```sh
zig build install-lapacke-lp64 -Doptimize=safe
# Or select the separate ILP64 artifact:
zig build install-lapacke-ilp64 -Doptimize=safe
```

The packages provide static/shared `zynum_lapacke_lp64` or
`zynum_lapacke_ilp64` libraries, `zynum_lapacke_{lp64,ilp64}.pc`, and
`include/zynum/lapacke/{lp64,ilp64}/lapacke.h` plus an ABI manifest. The header
provides standalone default types; an Intel SDK is not required. ILP64 consumers
must define `MKL_ILP64`; its pkg-config file supplies that flag. Select one width
per linked interface because the routine symbol names are identical.

Generated wrappers import the configured LAPACKE binding and borrow its Core,
Context and Resources. Default diagnostics use separately linked weak C
`LAPACKE_xerbla`/`xerbla_` definitions, with configured callback precedence and
one callback snapshot per operation. This does not establish other Fortran
character-length ABIs, full MKL error-control APIs or cross-library shared state.
The finite packages do not yet export the LAPACKE NaN-control functions.

The installed finite packages have passed independent C/C++ consumers for both
widths and static/shared linkage on Apple arm64. These checks establish only
the declared finite surface; complete LAPACK/LAPACKE and oneMKL compatibility
remain unfinished. Adding another vendor selection changes interface definitions
and translation over the same numerical owner and resource lifecycle.

Native C/C++ and Fortran consumers are explicit supplemental checks. They require a matching host/target and reject external execution through emulators. `test-checked-fortran` requires GNU Fortran; use `-Dchecked-gfortran=/absolute/path/to/gfortran` to select an existing compiler. The production libraries use `-Doptimize`; the consumer library and C/C++ tests use `-Dtest-optimize`. `check-checked-abi` checks generated-file drift and dynamic/static exports without running consumers.

For cross-object inspection, select compatible installed tools with `-Dchecked-nm=/absolute/path/to/llvm-nm` and `-Dchecked-readobj=/absolute/path/to/llvm-readobj`. Compilation and linking alone do not establish target runtime behavior. On Windows, the DLL is installed under `bin`, its import library under `lib`, and the separate static archive under `lib/static`. Select the static archive explicitly when static linkage is intended; `pkg-config zynum_checked` selects ordinary dynamic linkage.

Mach-O also exposes the two linker-provided data symbols `__dso_handle` and `_mh_dylib_header` after removing the platform leading underscore. They are recorded separately in the manifest, not declared as callable checked APIs. The exact export checker permits only those reviewed support-data names on Mach-O; ELF and restricted COFF have no additional allowed exports.

## One-owner LP64 LAPACKE and checked Sparse package

On Apple arm64, `zig build install-abplas-lp64 --release=safe -Dcpu=baseline`
installs `libzynum_abplas_lp64.a`, `libzynum_abplas_lp64.dylib`, the existing
LP64 LAPACKE and checked headers/manifests, and relocatable
`zynum_abplas_lp64.pc`. Select this library when combining the finite 48-entry
LP64 LAPACKE selection with the 128 mixed-index checked Sparse entries and
eight checked revision-1 entries. Use `pkg-config --cflags --libs
zynum_abplas_lp64`; the LAPACKE include directory provides `<lapacke.h>`.

The composition root borrows the exact same Core, LAPACKE binding and checked
Sparse module. The combined archive contains one default Context definition;
no second allocator, Executor or numerical implementation is introduced.
The shared library exports exactly 184 numerical entries and the two weak
LAPACKE diagnostics. It adds no public Context selector or operator ABI.
Existing separate packages remain available; linking those separate DSOs does
not provide the combined package's single-owner guarantee.

Relocated C11/C++20 consumers passed all 184 entries in both linkage modes,
including checked Sparse actions nested in LAPACKE error callbacks. C++ static
lifetime checks passed. A production-source ABPLaS regression executable links
`dgesv`, `zpotrf`, `dstev`, `dgelsd` and complex i64/i32 SpMV to this single
shared library. At 1/2/4 MPI ranks, 38/38/43 tests passed, with one Debug-only
assertion test skipped in each Release build. Five tests declared to require
four ranks run only at four ranks. These cover lattice, density mixing,
CheFSI and nonlocal projector boundaries, including physical Hamiltonian and
Lanczos checks. OpenBLAS still supplies BLAS and the independent `zheev`
oracle; FFTW, ELPA and PSolver remain. Full SCF and complete backend replacement
are not established. The existing GELSD range/invariant abort limitation is
unchanged. Other platforms and a combined ILP64 package remain unverified.

The installed checked CSR SpMV path now uses the internal synchronous operator
contract for `y = alpha*A*x + beta*y`, including independent offset/ordinal
widths and complex values. The CSR backend borrows the existing admission and
needs no extra scratch. Matrix-free callbacks use explicit caller workspace
for scaled accumulation; errors from that scratch-backed callback leave the
final output unchanged. Direct overwrite and fused-backend errors retain their
backend output semantics. Preflight rejects dimension, size, workspace and
alias violations without touching output, and beta zero does not read old y.
Zero alpha still validates CSR metadata. No admission, allocation or resource
pin is added. The existing 181-test Safe Sparse suite covers these boundaries;
all installed C/C++ entries and the selected ABPLaS MPI regressions pass through
the updated package. This establishes installed SpMV integration only: At that SpMV acceptance, SpMM
still called the existing shared Sparse kernel, and public operator ABI,
generalized CG and broader matrix-free algorithm integration remain pending.

The installed checked mixed-index CSR SpMM path now also borrows the internal
operator's multi-column action. It uses the existing native dense panels and
Sparse product kernel, one admitted Operation and no additional CSR workspace.
The internal panel contract accepts both row-major and column-major operands;
the existing checked C ABI keeps its column-major dense-view convention and
empty leading-dimension rules. Matrix-free callbacks pack one input column and
retain all product columns in explicit caller scratch before committing output.
Failure in a later column therefore preserves the entire final output. Padding,
storage/workspace tails, zero-coefficient semantics and metadata validation are
covered by the extended existing operator regressions; the complete Safe Sparse
root still passes 181 tests with unchanged test names.

Installed C11/C++20 static/shared consumers additionally pass 196 independent
dense-reference SpMM cases each: complex f32/f64, i64/i32 and u32/u64 indices,
normal/transpose/adjoint, 0/1/2/3/5 right-hand sides, complex scales and zero-scale
NaN nonreads, plus output-preserving rejection checks. All 184 combined entries,
shared-context lifetime checks and the same selected ABPLaS production-object
regression closure pass again at 1/2/4 MPI ranks. That application closure uses
the existing checked SpMV bridge; these runs do not establish an ABPLaS block
SpMM consumer or full SCF. Public operator ABI and reusable operator algorithms
remain pending. This stage adds no allocator, executor, handle or public symbol.

ABPLaS now has an explicit opt-in build selection for this installed package:
add its `lib/pkgconfig` directory to `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` and configure the existing
ABPLaS build with `-DABPLAS_ZYNUM_LP64=ON`, retaining the same compiler, materials,
Python validation environment and other dependency selections. The option is
off by default. Configure rejects a missing package or non-LP64 declaration
contract and checks the four required drivers plus mixed-index complex CSR
SpMV/SpMM linkage. It keeps the selected base BLAS provider and remaining
numerical dependencies. Current acceptance is Apple arm64 with OpenBLAS as that
base provider; a mixed MKL-base build has not been executed.

The actual ABPLaS `hmlt_csr.cpp` now uses checked complex f64 i64/i32 SpMV for
local overwrite and ghost accumulation under this selection, retaining its own
assembly, buffers and halo communication. The original implementation remains
selected when the option is off. LAPACKE includes explicitly use Zynum's finite
LP64 header. The selected finite library is placed before base-provider linker
options as well as ordinary libraries: the initial normal library ordering
still bound the four drivers to OpenBLAS and was rejected. Corrected actual
application and regression executables resolve all four required drivers and
mixed-index SpMV to the one installed `libzynum_abplas_lp64`; the test-only
`zheev` oracle continues to resolve to OpenBLAS.

Build-generated third-party configuration headers now precede source-tree
headers. This prevents a stale source-tree pseudopod config from redirecting
the actual build to an unavailable runtime data directory. The failed main
regression is preserved and excluded from acceptance.

The formal build passes the physical nonlocal-projector CTest at 1/2/4 MPI ranks
(24 passed and one Debug-only skip per run), 49 math tests at four ranks, and the
selected density/CheFSI/Ritz-state/ELPA-driver suites (49 passed at one/two ranks,
61 at four). Declared four-rank tests are excluded only from the lower-rank
selected solver invocations. A relocated ABPLaS runtime/SDK package rediscovers
Zynum with pkg-config and passes an independent linked consumer with verified
symbol origins. This supersedes the replacement-translation-unit limitation
above for these actual build/application boundaries. It does not establish an
ABPLaS block SpMM consumer, full SCF, complete BLAS/backend replacement, or
FFT/Hermitian eigensolver acceptance. The internal GELSD range/invariant terminal
fault boundary remains pending.

The formal opt-in build also passes the existing four-rank C8 cold-start
SCF-DIAG case against its unchanged frozen strict reference. It converges in
11 iterations with the configured joint energy/density stop and final refresh.
Energy and free-energy errors are 8.9e-16 Ha/atom; physical relevant eigenvalues
differ by at most 8.0e-10 Ha. Charge is 31.999999999999968 electrons and the
combined density residual is 3.52e-9 against the 1e-6 threshold. The validator
checks mixing, per-K electronic provenance and committed HDF5/sidecar output.
The frozen reference has no density field, so this is not a density-field or
cross-code comparison. This establishes this C8 full SCF case; other materials,
non-Gamma SCF, MKL-base builds and application block SpMM remain pending.

The same actual solver executable additionally passes 59 selected SCF
lifecycle, convergence, electronic-state and mixing tests at four MPI ranks,
including collective failure, publication and retry boundaries. A separate
installed GELSD probe passes 108 analytic DCT-factor cases across row/column
layout, square/tall/wide matrices, 8/32/64 columns, common scales 2^-1000/1/2^1000
and condition numbers 1/2^24. These finite numerical cases do not close the
internal range/invariant terminal-fault policy gap.

The formal opt-in package also passes the existing C8 non-Gamma DOS/CheFSI
case at crystal k=(0.25,0,0), independently at one and four MPI ranks. The
unchanged validator checks adaptive filtering, target/guard residuals, solve
budget, Hamiltonian application counts and finite band/DOS output. Four-rank
acceptance uses four solves, target residual 6.15e-9 Ha and guard residual
1.68e-7 Ha against 1e-6 Ha. The 24 band energies differ across rank counts by
at most 1.86e-15 Ha. The full-workspace residual remains diagnostic; this case
requires only target and verification-guard convergence. This is one non-Gamma
DOS/eigenpair workflow, not non-Gamma full SCF or a density-field comparison.

The next FFT implementation is grounded in nine current ABPLaS C++ plan sites:
real/complex 1D transforms, real half-spectrum 3D forward/inverse transforms
with x-fastest storage, and DCT-I (REDFT00). Callers retain their existing
normalization and MPI gather/scatter ownership. Chebyshev sampling uses length
32768; time-DOS uses power-of-two lengths of at least 1048576; spectrum lengths
and DCT lengths also require general dimensions. Plans and scratch must use
the shared Zynum data, memory, execution and handle contracts. This dependency
audit establishes requirements only; no Zynum FFT capability is delivered yet.

The shared Core now exposes an internal finite FFT foundation, using the same
complex scalar identity, storage range checks and injected Execution.Context
as the existing numerical modules. It covers arbitrary-length complex forward
and backward 1D transforms, real half-spectrum 1D transforms, DCT-I, and
contiguous complex/real half-spectrum 3D volumes in (z,y,x) order with x fastest.
Both directions are unnormalized; existing application normalization remains
caller-owned. Numerical work uses explicit widened f64/f128 complex scratch.
Output commits only after checked geometry, capacity, alias and finite-result
validation, preserving unused tails and final output on failure.

The internal managed facade admits one operation, or borrows a caller's already
admitted operation, and borrows either explicit workspace or the existing
ContextScratch lease. Captured allocator cleanup precedes resource-pin release
and operation end. Callback close, allocation/numerical failure, owner identity,
closing-context admission and operation/pin counter exhaustion are covered.
Plans remain numerical value descriptors. This foundation creates no separate
default, executor, allocator policy, persistent cache or handle registry.

The five numerical FFT tests and six actual-Core managed tests are registered in
the existing numerical-contract and LAPACK test roots. Compiler inventories and
body execution are recorded separately. The numerical source is identical to
the independently accepted 45-case FFTW comparison, including lengths 32768 and
1048576, odd/general dimensions, DCT-I and arbitrary real inverse half spectra.
This is internal native foundation acceptance. An installable MKL-first FFT ABI,
persistent descriptor/handle lifecycle, public IEEE/stride/in-place conventions
and actual ABPLaS FFT call replacement remain pending; the existing LP64
LAPACKE/Sparse exports retain their finite interfaces.


The internal FFT foundation also provides an affine persistent descriptor over
an existing ContextScratch metadata lease. It holds one pin across operations,
uses its original allocator for final metadata cleanup, and requires one live
same-Context operation for configuration, commit and execution. Invalid
geometry preserves the previous configuration and commit status; valid internal
reconfiguration clears commit. Executing an uncommitted descriptor or the wrong
transform domain fails before acquiring numerical scratch. Input/output/work
prefixes cannot overlap heap metadata or the descriptor's lease bookkeeping.
Explicit workspace adds no resource pin; automatic work uses the existing
ContextScratch mechanism. Deinitialization remains available after close and
frees metadata before its last pin, without a new admission or implicit drain.

Descriptor calls and destruction are externally serialized; copying a live
value does not retain it. No extra Context, allocator policy, thread pool,
handle registry or workspace cache is introduced. Nine transform directions in
both precisions, transactional configuration, another-owner refusal, allocation
and counter failures, callback close and captured-allocator cleanup are tested.
This is internal resource acceptance, not an installed vendor descriptor ABI.
Geometry reconfiguration is an internal facility: an MKL-facing DftiSetValue
must preserve the vendor's creation-only domain, precision, rank and lengths.
Public variadic/configuration/status rules, typed opaque shells, installation
and actual ABPLaS FFT replacement remain pending.

## Shared ownership and lifecycle boundary

The four public Zig packages are alias facades under `src/facades/` over the
same Core implementation owner. Fortran and CBLAS borrow Core through the one
`src/blas/abi/root.zig` adapter Module. The checked implementation also borrows
Core; Core never imports checked/interop adapters. Sharing requires the same
actual Module objects for a compatible artifact, target, optimization mode and
options, not merely equal source paths. Existing package declarations, checked
symbols and generated layouts are unchanged.

`src/interfaces.zig` defines an optional combined `zynum_interfaces` dynamic
artifact with the existing BLAS and checked exports and one default owner.
It adds no standard LAPACK/LAPACKE API and does not change the separate library
names or installation defaults. `build-combined-interfaces` builds and emits
this library without installing or executing it. Emission and linking require
separate native consumer and ABI checks before they can support compatibility
claims. The separate
`zynum_blas` and `zynum_checked` DSOs still have no shared-instance guarantee;
shared source or a common graph is not a cross-DSO allocator/handle protocol.

The handwritten `factor`, `solve` and `spmv` entries acquire and end one operation
token around all eight checked exports, including validation failures. Their
internal Cholesky and SpMV dispatchers borrow that token, retaining the checked
numerical validation without a second admission. Callers need no new token and
cannot choose or close that immortal default Context.

The thirty direct checked Zig computation entries (fifteen BLAS, nine LAPACK,
six Sparse) use the same default owner. Internal composition borrows the active
token; pure workspace queries do not admit work. The 156 legacy Fortran and 150
CBLAS numerical exports also admit once on that default Context, including
validation failures and empty calls. Their shared bodies and local helpers keep
the outer token through numerical work, output writes and serial fallback after
Executor refusal. Admission adds allocation-free counter updates and locking;
this is not a measured performance claim. An external call made from a callback
is a separate operation; no thread-local suppression skips its admission.

Checked Zig matrix products and Fortran/CBLAS GEMM carry that token's Executor
and scratch allocator through both real and complex computation. Complex 3M
and expanded-real subproducts, GEMV shortcuts and their contiguous scal/axpy
helpers share the same borrow. Standalone real and complex GEMV through the
checked Zig matrix-vector entries and shared Fortran/CBLAS bodies also carries
that borrow; checked GEMV workspace copy-in and copyback use it for COPY task
selection and submission. The checked Zig vector entries and computational
Level 1 Fortran/CBLAS routes also use the same Operation for task policy and
submission, including COPY and direct complex-return DOT. Vector `Into` calls
retain it through COPY plus computation and through exact-alias composition;
SCAL/AXPY/COPY shortcuts do not switch to a default executor. Scalar-only
ROTG/ROTMG remain scheduler-neutral under their existing outer admission.

The twelve s/d SYMV/SBMV/SPMV and c/z HEMV/HBMV/HPMV routes also borrow that
Operation through the Fortran bodies and their CBLAS callers. Their dense and
packed scratch, task policy and submission, and nested Hermitian Level 1 calls
use the same allocator and Executor. Busy-executor fallback retains the borrow;
already admitted work can finish after close is requested. Successful
scratch-backed work frees its scratch after tasks and final stores; a refused
task submission releases scratch before serial fallback. Both remain within
the outer operation, so close stays busy through each free call and operation
completion. This adds neither an operation nor a resource pin, and does not
make arbitrary borrowed memory safe.

Shared s/d/c/z TRMV/TRSV/TPMV/TBSV bodies now borrow the same Operation for
nested Level 1 work and selected real packed/band scratch. The captured
allocator frees scratch, and staged copyback completes, before the operation
ends; allocation refusal keeps the existing pre-write fallback. Shared
GER/GERU/GERC, SYR/SPR/SYR2/SPR2 and HER/HPR/HER2/HPR2 bodies also retain the
borrow through dense/packed scheduling and nested AXPY. Delegating CBLAS
branches share that path; local row-major helpers remain unchanged under
their original admission. Serial TBMV/TPSV leaves need no resource routing.
These are internal resource changes, with no new symbols, public Context
selector or change to numerical kernels, tuning gates or reduction order.

Row-major CBLAS HEMV/HBMV/HPMV uses the common dense/band/packed Hermitian view
with an explicit conjugated-matrix flag and opposite physical triangle.
Reflection, conjugation and real-only diagonal reads belong to the core; no
temporary matrix or extra admission is introduced. Zero beta replaces old
logical Y values without reading them, including when they contain NaNs.
Ignored imaginary diagonal values do not contribute. Existing validation
precedence, strides and untouched storage remain part of the interface contract.

Call-local GEMM/GEMV and symmetric/Hermitian MV scratch bypasses legacy TLS
caches. This scratch and the selected packed/band triangular scratch are freed
before the outer operation ends, including numerical fallback. Level 1
task/reduction arrays remain on the call stack, while the
shared Executor's captured-allocator worker storage may remain live until
drain/reset or internal Context close.
These paths add no checked ABI function or public Context selector. No-token
internal bridges keep their legacy default execution and allocation/cache
policy; outer admission alone does not migrate other unmodified Level 2/3
resource paths. This describes resource ownership, not a performance result
or complete vendor/target support.

The five service exports (`lsame_`, `xerbla_`, `xerbla_array_`,
`zynum_blas_shutdown` and `zynum_blas_shutdown_`) retain their existing semantics
without new admission. Shutdown requires caller-coordinated quiescence, releases
existing caller-local caches and resets the Executor for restart. It neither
terminally closes the Context nor waits for its operation/resource pins, and is
not a global drain or unload guarantee. This coverage does not establish a
complete vendor profile or lifetime coordination across separately linked DSOs.

Internal closable Contexts refuse new admissions and report busy while active
operations remain. They drain workers outside their gate, then report
waiting-resources until all pins are released before closed. `ContextScratch(T)` pins before allocation, rolls back
on failure, and returns memory to its captured allocator before unpinning;
zero-sized leases still retain a pin. It adds no managed buffer API to these
eight calls. The Context and allocator/callback backing state must outlive close
and every caller's return; pins do not validate raw pointer lifetimes.

### Internal LAPACKE services

Typed and raw POTRF/POTRS/GETRF/GETRS/GESV/STEV adapters borrow Core through `src/interop/lapacke_binding.zig`.
That binding imports one non-generic `lapacke_services.zig` configuration owner,
shared by its real/complex and i32/i64 specializations. NaN settings and callback
representation belong to the interface; Core never imports them. They create
no allocator, Context, Resources or Executor. Each shared managed call admits
once on an explicit internal Context, captures both callback bindings as one
record, and rebuilds allocator authority from the operation. The operation ends
after callbacks, copyback and cleanup. Default routes use the existing immortal
Context. Explicit borrowed-Services routes remain independent of shared config.

The raw routes share the typed call stages through `lapacke_access.zig`. They
retain nullable, initially unaligned pointers until the relevant scan or matrix
access; alignment and address arithmetic are checked at that stage. Row-major
scratch allocation, validation and copyback keep their existing order. Raw
memory faults stay distinct from LAPACK INFO and admission failures. A C export
must choose and verify its wire representation and fault policy separately.

The typed Reference-profile policy initializes NaN checking lazily on first
get: an unset `LAPACKE_NANCHECK` enables it, and the environment result is cached.
The zero/nonzero setter takes precedence; setting before the first get avoids
that environment read. Its ASCII decimal-prefix parser treats any nonzero
prefix as enabled even outside C-int range, an explicit Zynum extension rather
than a claim of vendor overflow behavior. Keep the process environment stable
during initialization; oneMKL lazy timing and parsing equivalence are not
established by this implementation.

Capturing callbacks does not snapshot the NaN flag. With scanning compiled in,
a high-level call reads the setting after accepting the layout and before its
scan; `_work`, compile-time no-scan routes and invalid layouts do not read it.
POTRF scans its selected triangle. POTRS checks the selected factor triangle
then the RHS, stopping at the first NaN result. GETRF scans the general matrix
and reports a NaN as INFO=-4 before its work-stage validation. Its output pivots
are never scanned or read. GETRS scans the full factor matrix, then the RHS;
their NaN results are INFO=-5 and INFO=-8 respectively. Its input pivots are not
part of NaN scanning. The existing typed admission and argument-order rules
remain distinct from the strict checked API.

GETRF reuses Core's IEEE LU policy and borrowed one-based i32/i64 pivot writer.
It checks output capacity, representability and mixed-width overlap before
factor or pivot stores. The column-major path validates scalar arguments before
its empty-shape return. Row-major conversion retains the Reference-profile
allocation and argument-check order, including empty shapes; its factor
copyback still occurs after positive singular INFO. Pivots are committed at
the core's original swap points, so INFO is never used as a pivot-copy count.
Managed routes keep all frees, callback returns and output writes within one
admitted call.

GETRS reuses the same LU solve policy for real/complex factors, one-based
i32/i64 pivots and multiple RHS. It translates `N`, `T` and `C` (adjoint), with
lowercase equivalents. Factors and pivots remain read-only. Used factor, RHS
and pivot prefixes must be pairwise disjoint, and every pivot must describe a
valid forward elimination swap; invalid storage or pivots remain separate
safety faults, not invented vendor INFO values. Scalar checks and empty returns
follow the adapter's existing stage order. In the row-major route, factor
scratch precedes RHS scratch, including the Reference-profile empty-case
allocation policy. Both are released in reverse order after RHS copyback;
failure of the second acquisition frees the first before the returning error
callback. Shared/default calls perform one admission spanning every callback,
copy and free. The finite generated GETRS exports delegate to this same route.

GESV composes the same LU factorization and normal solve under one admission.
It overwrites the factor matrix, one-based pivots and RHS; singular positive
INFO preserves the RHS, and zero RHS columns still factor the matrix. Row-major
factor scratch precedes RHS scratch and both are freed in reverse order. The
high-level entry scans the input matrix and RHS for NaNs before the work stage.
All four scalar types and both integer widths have installed C/C++ static/shared
consumer evidence, including inclusion after the pinned MKL declaration header.
Unmodified ABPLaS `src/math/geometry/lattice.cpp` also passed 36 independent
coordinate/reciprocal-lattice checks against the installed LP64 library. This is
a focused application harness, not the original ABPLaS test suite or full SCF
integration.

STEV uses one shared, allocation-free tridiagonal numerical core. The interface
adapts integer widths, row/column layouts, optional eigenvectors, NaN scanning,
workspace acquisition and diagnostic precedence through the existing Context
and Resources. Values-only calls do not reference Z or WORK. Positive INFO
counts unconverged off-diagonal entries; partial results retain the transformed
tridiagonal matrix. Checked finite-input behavior remains distinct from the
standard entrypoint's bounded IEEE arithmetic behavior.

The 21 additional tests cover analytic eigenvalues, residuals, orthogonality,
scaling, partial convergence, boundaries and callback-triggered closing.
Installed LP64/ILP64 C/C++ static/shared checks include standalone headers and
both inclusion orders with the pinned default-layout MKL headers. The actual
ABPLaS Lanczos source and original GTest fixture passed five single-rank and ten
two-rank cases; link inspection verifies Zynum `dstev` and independent OpenBLAS
`zheev`. Other ABPLaS paths and complete MPI application behavior are not implied.

GELSD uses the shared bidiagonal SVD and minimum-norm reconstruction cores,
with explicit workspace planning, row/column layout adaptation, returned rank
and singular values. Both real precisions provide high/work entrypoints at both
integer widths. High-level calls scan NaNs; work calls preserve their explicit
IEEE policy. Positive INFO reports actual unconverged bidiagonal entries.
Internal range/invariant faults remain separate from LAPACK INFO and terminate
after managed cleanup in these finite exports; this remains a release limitation,
not a claim of complete MKL behavior for every input.

The shared bidiagonal SVD now normalizes finite input in its existing widened
workspace before reduction/QR and restores singular and partial bidiagonal
values to original units. This fixes a reproduced large-scale convergence
failure: 16 of 144 installed LP64 high/work cases previously returned positive
INFO while an independent OpenBLAS GELSD reference converged. The updated
package passes all 144 tall/square cases and 96 additional wide/square cases,
covering both real precisions, both layouts, multiple RHS, normal/subnormal and
huge finite scales, analytic solutions and independent rank/singular checks.
A baseline-versus-candidate native regression also changes from failure to
success, and all 30 SVD/minimum-norm/rank-least-squares root tests pass. The
workspace/ownership model, finite output range checks, explicit IEEE policy and
actual-unfinished-edge INFO semantics remain unchanged. This closes the
reproduced scale failure; internal range/invariant termination remains a
separate unresolved release limitation.

The native Safe LAPACK suite passes 286 tests. Eight relocated C/C++ consumers
cover both integer widths and static/shared linkage. The original ABPLaS density
mixing tests pass with the installed LP64 static and shared libraries, with
symbol inspection confirming Zynum DGELSD. Nonfinite reference probes describe
OpenBLAS observations, not a portable or complete vendor contract.

The installed ZPOTRF also passes the original CheFSI full-space and rank-deficient
single-rank tests with static/shared linkage, plus the four-rank distributed
full-space test with the shared library. Application and test support sources
were recompiled. ELPA and other mathematical providers remain in that fixture;
these results validate the replaced Cholesky boundary, not all of ABPLaS.

On Apple arm64 the dynamic package is linked from the repacked static archive
with the system linker, a manifest-derived export list and the configured minimum
macOS version. It exports the 48 declared routines and two default diagnostics,
not the linker's internal `__dso_handle`. The application fixture exercises C++
static destruction that exposed the previous dynamic packaging conflict.

The `lapacke` and `fortran_returning_test` callback channels are independent.
Replacement and capture synchronize the whole function/userdata record;
callbacks execute outside that gate. A null channel is a returning, no-output
sink in this internal profile. This is neither a standard XERBLA export nor a
Fortran STOP implementation. Replacing callbacks returns the old record but
does not authorize reclaiming its userdata or code: both must remain alive
until every invocation that captured them returns. Callers also synchronize
their own callback state. The finite generated LAPACKE consumers supply per-call
default handlers when a configured channel is null; direct internal calls retain
the no-output behavior. These finite exports do not make a full vendor profile ready.

### Internal Sparse handle slice

`src/interop/mkl_sparse_binding.zig` borrows the same Core's Pattern, Object,
Product, Execution and Resources. One interface shell family has eight typed payloads:
four real/complex scalar types crossed with signed i32/i64 indices. These are
private semantic tags, not Intel's `sparse_matrix` layout or wire enums. The
current routes create a borrowed CSR/CSC handle, export the same format,
multiply a general or supported square structured matrix by a vector and
destroy it. They add no standard C
symbols, vendor status mapping or profile readiness. Shell-level copy and value
update APIs remain future work.

The raw lifecycle adapter uses the same shell and common control as the typed
routes. A null ends pointer selects a contiguous major-plus-one offset array
when the major dimension is nonzero; a nonnull ends pointer must supply a real
split-range prefix. Empty-array pointer tokens, including null, are preserved
without dereferencing or aligning them. Arbitrary nonnull dummy ends pointers
are outside this input contract. Export checks all seven output slots, their
mutual overlap and overlap with borrowed data and metadata before any store;
the operation remains active through the last store. These sequential stores
are not an atomic publication protocol, so callers still synchronize access.

Creation admits one operation and captures its allocator. It allocates one
common managed control and then one shell; only the control holds a resource
pin, regardless of retained control references. If either allocation fails,
cleanup frees acquired metadata before unpinning and leaves the output handle
unchanged. Successful creation commits the output once without reading its old
value. Destruction needs no new admission, so it remains available while the
Context is closing. It frees the shell, releases the shell's control reference,
and on final release frees the control before the pin is released. Borrowed
arrays are neither read nor freed during destruction. Context, allocator and
callback/code backing must outlive every active stack, including free callbacks.

Inputs are truthful mutable slices. The shell retains that provenance rather
than casting a read-only common export to mutable; no owned snapshot or
read-only control can enter this export route. Same-format export allocates
nothing, revalidates borrowed metadata on every call and commits its output
record only on success. Exported slices retain no reference and extend no
lifetime. Arrays stay caller-owned and must remain live and stable during
access. Handle/control/array access requires external serialization; copying a
handle does not retain it, and allocator callbacks must not reenter the same
handle. Live originating handles are required; tag/alignment checks do not
make stale or arbitrary pointers safe.

This typed domain supports zero/one bases and split starts/ends, including
shifted views into a common offsets array. Intervals must be monotone and
nonoverlapping; physical gaps, duplicate ordinals and stored ordering remain.
Only the required prefixes are retained; unused capacity is excluded from
output-alias checks. The explicit ordinals/value backing prefix must cover
even empty interval endpoints. Broader common Pattern intervals and documented
vendor null/dummy-end forms remain outside this slice; that does not classify
them as invalid oneMKL inputs. Lifecycle calls perform no scalar conversion,
sorting or value arithmetic, so borrowed numerical bits are preserved. The allocator-only
common control remains unmanaged; the shell uses the actual managed control
and introduces no separate pool or default owner.

### Internal Sparse matrix-vector adapter

Typed and raw CSR/CSC multiplication reuse the same handle family and
the common Product implementation. The raw entry admits one operation on the
handle's captured Context, translates N/T/H and the descriptor, and revalidates
borrowed structure before acquiring the required vector prefixes. The admitted
typed entry checks dimensions and output overlap with x, captured arrays, shell
and control before any numerical write. It calls the common product directly;
it creates no temporary matrix, allocation, resource pin or second admission.

The internal descriptor is a semantic record, not a C layout. General matrices
ignore mode and diagonal bits. Square symmetric, Hermitian and triangular
matrices select the lower or upper stored half; diagonal matrices ignore the
half selector. Each supports stored or implicit unit diagonals. FULL-half,
block-structured descriptors and rectangular structured domains remain
unsupported; unknown operation or descriptor values are errors.
Complex H conjugates matrix values; real H has the same mathematics as T.
Both index widths and bases retain the same storage order, duplicates and
physical gaps as lifecycle calls.

All structured routes call one common coordinate implementation. It filters
the original stored half before applying N/T/H, conjugates Hermitian mirrored
entries once and ignores the imaginary diagonal component. A unit diagonal
uses the input directly even when no entries are stored; stored diagonal
values are not read. Ignored numerical values do not bypass metadata, capacity
or alias checks. These routes add no allocation or additional Context admission.

Every call rechecks borrowed metadata. Callers keep the handle, Context, arrays
and vector storage live and stable through return. Raw pointers supply exact
required prefixes, not discoverable allocation capacities. Empty prefixes do
not require alignment or dereference; nonempty vectors remain required when
alpha is zero. Zero alpha skips unused matrix/vector numerical reads, and zero
beta skips old output reads. NaN/Inf propagate through the shared numerical
contract. Preflight errors preserve output. These internal rules do not by
themselves establish standard C calling conventions or oneMKL error precedence.

### Shared sparse panel computation

The common Product implementation now uses borrowed regular dense panels for
one or more RHS columns. Panel geometry supports row-major and column-major
storage with native-width dimensions; it preserves the existing general and
square structured semantics while sharing sparse traversal across at most two
columns at a time. Empty panels avoid unused offset arithmetic. Padding and
unused tails are not output elements, and callers retain geometry, alias and
lifetime responsibilities. This computational route allocates nothing and
creates no Context, allocator or Executor.

The existing checked CSR SpMM entry delegates to this common route after its
unchanged validation and column-major layout checks. Existing vector routes
use the same numerical traversal with one column. Internal typed and raw handle
MM entries now use these panels for CSR/CSC, real/complex values and i32/i64
indices. They use one layout for both dense operands. Zero-based row-major and
one-based column-major panels accept the supported general and square
structured operations; the other two base/layout combinations accept only
normal general CSR multiplication. This interface restriction does not narrow
the common panel implementation.

Typed and raw MM share scalar checks, borrowed metadata revalidation, the
configuration filter and panel geometry. Raw calls resolve the input prefix
then the output prefix only after both extents have been checked. Empty panels
avoid unused offset arithmetic; zero alpha or zero RHS columns do not bypass
metadata, configuration, capacity or alias checks. Before any output store,
the output's bounding span, including internal padding, must be disjoint from
the input span, sparse arrays, shell and control. Inputs, output padding and
unused tails remain unchanged. The handle, Context, borrowed arrays and dense
storage must remain live and stable until return. The admitted preparation
record is valid only for that same handle and operation; it is not a reusable
validation cache.

MM admits once on the handle's captured Context and calls the existing common
Product directly. It allocates no temporary storage, retains no additional
control reference and acquires no resource pin. These are internal typed/raw
contracts, with separate safety errors; they do not establish oneMKL status or
error-priority equivalence. The finite C packages below forward to these same
contracts; a complete vendor profile remains unavailable.

### Finite Sparse C packages

On Apple arm64 with the default C type representations, build either integer
model with `zig build install-sparse-lp64 -Doptimize=safe` or
`zig build install-sparse-ilp64 -Doptimize=safe`. Each package installs a static
library, a shared library, a standalone `mkl_spblas.h`, an ABI manifest and a
relocatable `zynum_sparse_lp64.pc` or `zynum_sparse_ilp64.pc` file. Use the
selected pkg-config entry for include paths, link flags and the ILP64 macro.
Both models export the same names: do not link them together.

Each package provides 25 functions: CSR/CSC create and export, MV and MM for
single/double real and complex values, plus handle destruction. Generated
wrappers borrow the configured `mkl_sparse_binding_mod`; they create no second
numerical owner, allocator, thread runtime or workspace manager. Storage is
borrowed: arrays must remain live while the handle is used, and destruction
does not free those arrays. Export returns the original storage pointers.

The supported descriptors are general, square symmetric, Hermitian,
triangular and diagonal. Block descriptors and full stored-triangle mode are
unsupported. Normal, transpose and conjugate-transpose operations and both
dense layouts use the existing checked semantic adapters. Integer widths
apply to both offsets and ordinals in this ordinary interface; the ABPLaS
mixed-index route is supplied by the additive checked Sparse package and
the combined LP64 package described above.

Custom complex definitions, packed structs and shortened enums are rejected.
When combining SDK and generated headers, include the SDK Sparse header first.
This finite target contract does not establish full MKL support or identical
vendor error precedence. Installed, relocated C11/C++17 consumers have passed
both linkage modes and integer widths; other platforms remain unverified.

## ABI decisions

All descriptors and the result are **passed by value**. Buffer fields are a pointer plus signed 64-bit **element count**, never byte count. Dense descriptors add signed 64-bit rows, columns, and leading dimension. CSR descriptors contain separate const buffers for row offsets, column indices, and values, plus signed 64-bit rows and columns. These are small C-compatible value aggregates; no descriptor or info-output pointers need secondary validation or can alias the numerical result. C and Zig preserve input-pointer constness; Fortran uses `type(c_ptr)` and caller discipline.

This interface explicitly targets 64-bit-pointer ABIs. Generated C/C++ and Zig guards assert descriptor sizes, alignments, and every field offset against the schema's fixed 64-bit layout model. Generated Fortran checks `c_sizeof` and every offset using `c_loc`; actual calls test aggregate argument and return lowering. Native consumer execution and foreign-target link checks are distinct evidence; successful cross-linking does not validate runtime calling conventions or numerical behavior. Windows `.def` plus Zig `dll_export_fns=false` restricts the DLL to the eight declared application exports while preserving its normal startup/TLS machinery. Neither `-fno-entry` nor single-threaded compilation is required.

Flags and status use fixed `int32_t`, not C enums or character conventions. Flags are LOWER=1, UPPER=2, NORMAL=0, TRANSPOSED=1. The scalar and index types are selected by the function suffix. Fortran interfaces use `bind(C)` and `value` exactly; no hidden character-length argument or trailing-underscore ABI convention exists here.

The returned 16-byte `result` is `{ int32_t status; int32_t reserved; int64_t info; }`. `reserved` is always zero. `info` is zero except on numerical failure, where it is the one-based Cholesky pivot/row index. Status values are explicitly fixed in the schema: OK=0; INVALID_FLAG=1; INVALID_DIMENSION=2; INVALID_LEADING_DIMENSION=3; BUFFER_TOO_SMALL=4; NULL_POINTER=5; MISALIGNED_POINTER=6; SIZE_OVERFLOW=7; DIMENSION_MISMATCH=8; ALIASING_NOT_ALLOWED=9; INVALID_SPARSE_STRUCTURE=10; NONFINITE_INPUT=11; NUMERICAL_FAILURE=12; INVALID_LENGTH=13; INTERNAL_ERROR=14 (unexpected implementation error, not a numerical status). The interface does not promise which error wins when multiple arguments are invalid.

## Checked contract

- Signed lengths/dimensions must be nonnegative. Dense dimensions and leading dimensions also must fit the underlying Zynum signed 32-bit BLAS view. Dense storage is column major with span `(cols-1)*ld+rows`; zero rows or columns require no elements and accept nonnegative `ld`, including zero. Nonempty shapes require `ld >= rows`. `storage.length` may include padding or an unused tail; those remain untouched.
- Before creating Zig slices, the adapter checks element-byte multiplication, `PTRDIFF_MAX` bounds, null positive-length pointers, scalar/index alignment, and pointer-end addition. A zero-length pointer is ignored, so null is allowed. Every pointer is preflighted before any CSR metadata read or numerical operation. It cannot establish that an arbitrary address really names a live accessible allocation: callers must supply truthful lengths and readable inputs/writable outputs, keep buffers alive, and avoid concurrent mutation. This is the ordinary memory-ownership requirement of this checked C interface.
- Cholesky factors require square matrices. Only the selected triangle is read or overwritten. Nonfinite selected input is rejected before mutation. Solve checks factor/RHS dimensions, finite factor/RHS values, and prohibited physical-span overlap. Input factors, opposite triangles, padding, and trailing storage are preserved.
- Argument/structure/nonfinite/alias errors leave numerical storage unchanged. A Cholesky numerical failure may retain partial factorization or substitution; a nonpositive solve diagonal is detected before RHS mutation. `NUMERICAL_FAILURE` plus `info` is distinct from an invalid argument. No rollback allocation occurs.
- CSR is zero based. Row offsets have **exactly rows+1 entries**, start at zero, are nondecreasing, and end at `values.length`; column-index length equals value length, all indices are below `cols`, and nnz must fit the chosen unsigned index type. Unsigned indices are selected by the symbol, independently of signed descriptor counts. Fortran has no unsigned interoperable integer kind: the example uses nonnegative `integer(c_int32_t)`/`integer(c_int64_t)` buffers within their signed positive range, whose representations match these unsigned values; a portable full-range unsigned Fortran convenience API is deferred.
- SpMV vectors have **exact** effective lengths (normal: x=cols,y=rows; transpose: x=rows,y=cols). Unsorted columns and duplicate entries are allowed and visited in storage order. `y = alpha*op(A)*x + beta*y`; beta=0 does not read old y, and alpha=0 does not read numerical inputs but still validates structure and aliases. Sparse arithmetic follows the public module's floating-point propagation; unlike Cholesky, it does not reject nonfinite numerical values.
- Every Sparse call rechecks borrowed CSR structure. Output cannot overlap x, CSR values, row offsets, or column indices; input-input overlap is allowed. Checks occur before result writes, including zero-alpha calls. All checks are present in Fast mode too.

## Consumer checks and scope

The suite exercises all eight exports in all three consumer languages; C and C++ share the same strictly compiled test source. It checks independent reconstruction/solve residuals for both triangles and scalar types, sentinel padding, CSR normal/transpose and duplicates, both index widths, all descriptor layouts, invalid flags/dimensions/capacity/null/alignment/size/address arithmetic, invalid changed CSR structure, output overlap with every input class, no mutation on failures, empty storage, and zero-scale behavior. Run these consumers against the library and target configuration being used; their results are supplemental to the canonical Zig test inventory.

Consumer execution, export/layout checks and canonical inventory validation
provide distinct evidence. Acceptance requires results bound to the exact
library, source and target configuration. A successful build or foreign link
does not establish runtime behavior, full compatibility or completion of the
consumer suite.

Revision 1 covers the eight functions listed above. LU/QR wrappers, CSC/COO
conversion wrappers, complex arithmetic, batched operations and a general
LAPACKE interface are future work for this ABI. This ABI is experimental;
consult the manifest and release notes before depending on layout or symbol
stability.
